title: Policy-Scoped Compliance Intake Gateway with Automated Evidence Sampler
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a policy-scoped intake gateway that automatically categorizes incoming security & compliance asks (SOC2/ISO, HIPAA, GDPR, DPA, vendor questionnaires) by regulatory scope and business impact, then produces a prioritized routing decision and a minimal evidence bundle sampler. The gateway should: 1) surface an SLA estimator (time to respond with evidence) based on account tier, region, and ask complexity; 2) create a canonical case record for downstream SME routing (security, legal, infra); 3) attempt automated evidence sampling from existing artifacts (Confluence, shared drives, infra dashboards) and attach a confidence score; 4) include a feedback loop so SMEs can correct classification and evidence selection, improving the model over time.
acceptance_criteria: Incoming asks are auto-classified into at least four scopes: SOC2/ISO, Privacy (GDPR/DPA), Health (HIPAA), and Vendor Questionnaires with >=75% initial accuracy in a 200-ticket holdout sample.
SLA estimator returns a suggested response window (hours/days) and a rationale string (e.g., 'High ARR + HIPAA + EU region') for >90% of tickets.
Automated evidence sampler attaches at least one relevant artifact for 60% of matched asks with a confidence score and a source link.
SME routing rules can be configured by product/region and default to named queues when no exact match is found.
An audit log captures classification, sampler results, routing decision, and SME overrides for each ticket.
A lightweight UI in the intake console shows the classifier output, sampled evidence, and an 'override' action for SMEs.
Privacy checks ensure no PII is exfiltrated by sampler; sampler only attaches links or metadata unless the account explicitly permits artifact copying.
Documentation and runbook published in Confluence with triage examples and failure modes.
Integration tests demonstrating end-to-end flow with a synthetic dataset and a CanOps checklist for on-call handoff.

decision_log: 2026-02-22: Decided to use a hybrid classifier: deterministic rules for region-sensitive flags (e.g., EU data residency, HIPAA) plus a light ML model for free-text mapping.
2026-02-28: Sampler will prefer metadata (link, title, excerpt) and only copy document content if account legal explicitly permits; default is link-only to meet privacy constraints.

2026-03-04: SLA estimator algorithm will be transparent and auditable; initial formula: base SLA by account tier + complexity multiplier (questionnaire length + regulatory scope) + regional adjustment.
2026-03-08: Rollout strategy: beta for 10 pilot accounts (mix of SMB and enterprise) for 4 weeks before org-wide opt-in.
2026-03-09: Logging and observability: add per-ticket telemetry (classification confidence, sampler success/fail, routing queue) to console-2026.04 dashboards.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Sampler may surface incorrect internal documents leading to leaked context. Mitigation: default to link-only, add internal-only tag filter, and require legal opt-in before copying artifacts.
Risk: Classifier misroutes high-severity asks. Mitigation: human-in-the-loop review for high ARR or high regulatory-scope tickets for first two months; fast override action in UI.
Risk: SLA estimator gives unrealistic expectations. Mitigation: conservative default SLA and a 'commitment review' step where Ops confirms estimated timelines for P0/P1s.
Risk: GDPR/HIPAA nuance missed by model. Mitigation: curated rule set maintained by Security + quarterly audit and sampled accuracy checks.
